items.detail: Sanctioned exceptions: historical release notes, progress logs, design docs, and immutable eval-run artifacts. Do NOT edit (per surgical-changes rule); excluded from the zero-ref acceptance grep. New CHANGELOG 5.0.0 entry will ADD gemini/opencode mentions (breaking-change #10) — expected.

verify_commands: test ! -e .gemini && test ! -e .opencode && test ! -e tests/integration/opencode && test ! -f tests/node/test-opencode-plugin.js && test ! -f docs/README.gemini.md && test ! -f docs/README.opencode.md && test ! -f skills/arc-using/references/opencode-tools.md && echo WS1-DELETES-OK
npm run build:website && git diff --exit-code website/page/hero.js website/page/sections.js && echo WEBSITE-REBUILT-IN-SYNC
risks: check:docs blind spots: scripts/check-doc-refs.js scans only skills/, docs/guide/, agents/, templates/, hooks/, README.md — dangling references in CONTRIBUTING.md:335-336, docs/README.md:42, docs/README.codex.md, .claude/rules/plugin.md, .claude/skills/arc-releasing/, and .claude/workflows/ break SILENTLY. The zero-ref grep (verify command 2) is the only gate for those.

tests/node/run-tests.js auto-discovers test files, so deleting test-opencode-plugin.js can never fail a build — but it also means an accidental partial delete (plugin kept, test deleted, or vice versa where the test remains and the plugin is gone) surfaces only via test:node failure in the second case and not at all in the first. Delete both together.

.claude/workflows/arc-release-audit.js:195 embeds a grep whose path list includes .opencode/plugins/arcforge.js — if unedited, the release-audit subagent's command errors at the NEXT release, not in CI (no test covers this file).

arc-releasing SKILL.md is loaded by trigger description ('10-file version bump') — if the frontmatter count is not updated, the next release session is steered by a stale contract; nothing mechanical asserts the count matches check-version-sync.js's LOCATIONS length.

Version-sync only shrinks 10→9 in this workstream (the .opencode entry is the sole gemini/opencode entry); the decision record's '~6' requires separate non-WS1 decisions (e.g. website consolidation) — don't let the plan claim ~6 from this PR alone.

Editing evals/scenarios/eval-arc-using-read-only-nonactivation.md fixture text changes eval inputs; its recorded results in evals/results/ no longer correspond. Safe only because D5 declares a new baseline epoch — sequence this edit before regenerating evals/benchmarks/latest.json.

Forgetting `npm run build:website` after the .jsx edits leaves committed hero.js/sections.js with GEMINI/OPENCODE strings — check:versions still passes (version patterns intact), so only the grep + rebuild-diff verify commands catch it.

hooks/inject-skills/main.sh comment edit sits next to content asserted by tests/skills/test_minimal_toolkit_docs.py (posture lines, no-smuggling guards) — touching more than the comment fails pytest loudly, but a careless reflow of bootstrap.txt would change the injected bytes for real sessions.

External users with existing Gemini/OpenCode symlink installs get no runtime warning — their symlinks dangle silently after updating the clone. Per D1 (N=1, hard break) this is accepted; the CHANGELOG breaking-changes entry is the only notice.
